# Start, configure, maintain and stop the hub

## Intent

An operator runs the hub from one binary, one configuration file and one data directory. This package gives `parleyd` its life as a process: it reads and strictly validates its configuration, opens its data, hands the operator a first admin token, resumes durable work, runs hourly maintenance, stops within a bounded time, never lets a credential leave in text, and can snapshot its data while it runs. Every later package plugs its configuration keys, schema, start-up work, background work and maintenance tasks into what this package builds.

## Goals

- `parleyd` reads `config.toml` from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or the working directory, replaces `${NAME}` references in string values, and stops the start with an error that names the key on invalid TOML, an unknown section, an unknown key or an invalid value. A missing file means all defaults.
- `parleyd` creates its data directory (mode 0700) and workspace root, opens a transactional store and an analytical store, and brings both to the current schema on every start without a separate step.
- `parleyd --admin-email=a@x` on a new hub writes an admin token file (mode 0600), logs its path and exits 0 without serving; the hub refuses to start while the file exists; `--reset-admin-token` replaces the token.
- The start runs in one fixed order (configuration, data, bootstrap, resumed durable work, maintenance loop, listener), and any failure before listening exits 1 with one error line on stderr.
- The maintenance loop runs one pass right after start and then one every hour, runs its tasks in a fixed order, never overlaps passes, and a failing task never stops the others.
- On SIGTERM or SIGINT the process exits with status 0 at most 30 seconds after the signal, after giving requests 15 seconds and each piece of background work its own grace.
- One scrubbing function removes credentials from any text: known secret values and hub credentials become `[redacted]`, user information is removed from URLs, and the text is cut to 1024 bytes. The hub's logger applies it to every line.
- `parleyd backup <directory>` writes a consistent snapshot of the data of a running hub into an empty directory and exits 1 when the directory is not empty.

## Non-goals

- The listener, `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/version` as endpoints, the 15-second grace for in-flight requests, `--help` and the refusal of an unknown flag as first delivered: package 01 hub_skeleton. This package extends that start and stop.
- The body limit, the rate limit, the access-log line and the behaviour of `Idempotency-Key` themselves: package 02 http_api_conventions. This package reads `[server].max_body_size`, `[limits].requests_per_minute` and `[logging].log_health_probes` and hands the values to the server, and it gives the server a place in the transactional store for its idempotency records.
- Authenticating a request with the admin token, and using the OAuth providers this package reads from configuration: package 04 authentication_and_login.
- The configuration keys of other sections (`[forks]`, the other keys of `[limits]`, `[events]`, `[audit]`, `[sessions]`, `[webhooks]`, `[git]`, `[scm]`, `[changes]`, `[land]`, `[awareness]`, `[secrets]`, `[sandbox]` and its tables): the package that owns each registers its keys with the loader this package builds (packages 10 to 53).
- The tables of every feature: each package registers its own schema steps with the store this package builds.
- What each maintenance task does (retention, secret re-encryption, claim cleanup, forge delivery pruning, token binding sweep, patch purge, fork expiry, sandbox record cleanup): packages 51 audit_query_and_retention, 39 secrets, 30 awareness, 43 forge_webhook_ingress, 08 workspace_bound_tokens, 38 carry_patch_rerere_and_maintenance, 16 task_fork_lifetime and 47 sandbox_lifecycle_and_checkpoints. This package runs whatever is registered.
- What is resumed at start (clones, restacks, land attempts, rebuild jobs, sandbox provisioning) and the reconciliation of refs with records: packages 10, 24, 25, 33, 45 and 54. This package runs the registered start hooks in order.
- The sandbox runtime check at start (SBX-FR-003): package 44 sandbox_runtime_and_profiles, as a start hook.
- Closing event streams and stopping rebuild jobs at shutdown: packages 52 durable_event_log_and_stream and 33 rebuild_jobs. This package gives them the shutdown notification and the grace mechanism.
- The `git` version check at start (NFR-004), the guarantee that a newer binary opens the data of the previous release (NFR-003) with its tests, restoring a snapshot and the proof that a hub started on a restored snapshot starts cleanly under load (NFR-007), log fields beyond those named here (NFR-042), container images and manifests: package 54 operations_and_packaging.
- `PARLEY_SECRETS_KEY` and `PARLEY_SECRETS_KEY_PREVIOUS`: package 39 secrets. Proxy variables are honoured by the standard library's HTTP client in the packages that make outgoing calls.
- The client configuration file and the `parley` environment variables: package 09 cli_foundation.
- Refusing a second `parleyd` on the same data: not covered by this package; the PRD says only that it is not supported (§3.3.1).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Package 01 hub_skeleton delivers `cmd/parleyd` with a run function, `internal/server` with the three unauthenticated endpoints, a list of readiness probes and a 15-second shutdown grace, and `internal/buildinfo`. Until this package, `parleyd` listens on `0.0.0.0:8080`, has no configuration, no data and no background work.

The source PRD (`docs/prd/03_platform.md`) puts the process's life in PLAT-FR-001 to PLAT-FR-005, scrubbing in PLAT-FR-098 and configuration in §3.9; `docs/prd/15_non_functional.md` adds the one-process, embedded-store model (NFR-001, NFR-002), automatic schema evolution (NFR-003), the backup command (NFR-007), restart survival (NFR-013) and the maintenance guarantee (NFR-043).

This package builds in these places:

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `internal/config/` | the configuration loader: location, TOML, environment references, the key registry, the keys of §3.9 |
| `internal/store/` | the two embedded stores: path resolution, open, schema steps, transactions, snapshot |
| `internal/scrub/` | the scrubbing function (new directory; a leaf that imports nothing of the project) |
| `internal/identity/admin.go` | the admin settings: bootstrap e-mail, admin token generation, the stored hash |
| `internal/maintenance/` | the maintenance loop and its task registry |
| `internal/hub/` | the composition of the process (new directory): start order, start hooks, background work, logger, shutdown, the backup command |
| `cmd/parleyd/` | `main`: flags, the `backup` subcommand, exit status |

## Requirements

### Flags and the subcommand (PLAT-FR-001, §3.9 "Server flags")

`parleyd` takes `--admin-email <string>` and `--reset-admin-token`. `--help` prints usage on stdout and exits 0. An unknown flag prints usage on stderr and exits 2. The one subcommand is `parleyd backup <directory>`; any other positional argument, and `backup` with no directory or more than one, prints usage on stderr and exits 2. Nothing is loaded, opened or bound in those cases.

### Configuration file (§3.9)

**Location.** `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set and non-empty, otherwise `./config.toml`. The directory of that file is the **config dir**; it also holds the `admin_token` file. A missing file means all defaults. The file is read once, at start. A file that exists and cannot be read is a start error that names its path.

**Strictness.** Invalid TOML, an unknown section, an unknown key or an invalid value stops the start with an error that names the key (as `section.key`; for invalid TOML, the line). The process exits 1 with one error line on stderr.

**Environment references.** `${NAME}` inside a string value is replaced by the environment variable `NAME`. A reference to an unset variable is a start error that names the variable and the key. `$$` yields a literal `$`. A variable that is set to the empty string yields the empty string. References are replaced after the file is parsed and only in string values, so a variable's content can never add a key or a section. The replaced value is validated like a literal one.

**Keys this package owns.**

| Section | Key | Type | Default | Valid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[server]` | `bind` | string | `"0.0.0.0"` | non-empty |
| `[server]` | `port` | int | `8080` | 0–65535; 0 picks a free port |
| `[server]` | `external_url` | string | `""` | empty, or an absolute `http` or `https` URL |
| `[server]` | `max_body_size` | string | `"1MB"` | a positive integer followed by `KB`, `MB` or `GB`, case-insensitive, powers of 1024 |
| `[database]` | `path` | string | see below | non-empty |
| `[workspace]` | `path` | string | see below | non-empty |
| `[workspace]` | `workers` | int | `4` | at least 1 |
| `[logging]` | `level` | string | `"info"` | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`, case-insensitive |
| `[logging]` | `log_health_probes` | bool | `false` | |
| `[limits]` | `requests_per_minute` | int | `600` | 0 or more; 0 turns the limit off |
| `[[oauth.providers]]` | `name` | string | required | `github` or `google`; unique among the providers |
| `[[oauth.providers]]` | `client_id`, `client_secret` | string | required | non-empty |
| `[[oauth.providers]]` | `authorize_url`, `token_url`, `userinfo_url` | string | the provider's public endpoints | absolute `http` or `https` URL |

**Keys other packages own.** A later package registers each key it owns with the loader: section, key, type, default and a validation rule. A key in the file that nobody registered is unknown. Registering the same `section.key` twice is an error at start.

**Sections other packages own as a whole.** A later package may instead register a whole section by name with a validator of its own. The loader does not check the keys of such a section. When the file holds the section, the loader hands the validator the section's parsed content, after the environment references in its string values are replaced, and the validator returns one error that reports all the section's failures together; that error stops the start. When the file does not hold the section, the validator is not called and the configuration reports the section as absent. Registering a section twice, or as a whole when keys are registered in it, is an error at start.

### Data directory and stores (§3.9 `[database]`, `[workspace]`; NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003)

`database.path` defaults to `./data/parley.db`, or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/parley.db` when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set and non-empty. A bare file name is placed under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` when that is set. `workspace.path` defaults to `./data/workspaces`, or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/workspaces`, with the same resolution. The directory of the database file is the **data directory**.

At start the hub creates the data directory with mode 0700 and the workspace root, opens the transactional store at `database.path` and the analytical store beside it, and applies every schema step that the data has not yet had, in order, each in one transaction. A second start applies none. A step that fails is rolled back, the steps before it stay, and the start stops with exit status 1 and an error that names the step. A data directory that cannot be created, or a store file that cannot be opened, stops the start the same way, naming the path.

Work on the transactional store runs in transactions: a transaction whose function returns without error is committed, and one whose function returns an error or panics leaves no trace. Two transactions running at the same time both complete; neither fails because the other is running (PLAT-FR-019).

`GET /readyz` answers `200 {"status":"ready"}` while both stores answer a query and `503 {"status":"not ready"}` when one does not (§3.5, §3.10).

### Start (PLAT-FR-002)

The server loads and validates its configuration, opens its data, runs the bootstrap, resumes durable work, starts the maintenance loop and then listens on `[server].bind:[server].port`. Durable work is resumed through **start hooks** that later packages register; they run in registration order, each to completion, before the listener is bound. Any failure before listening stops the process with exit status 1 and one error line on stderr, with no `listening` line.

When it starts listening, the server logs one line with `msg` `listening`, the bound address as `addr`, the configuration path as `config` and the data directory as `data_dir`.

Logs are JSON lines on stderr. A line below `[logging].level` is not written. The configured body limit, request rate and health-probe logging are handed to the HTTP server.

### Bootstrap (PLAT-FR-003, PLAT-US-01)

The hub is **bootstrapped** once an admin token hash is stored. The token file is `<config dir>/admin_token`.

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| not bootstrapped, no flags | start normally, without an admin token |
| not bootstrapped, `--admin-email` | store the e-mail, generate the token, write the file, exit |
| `--reset-admin-token` (bootstrapped or not) | generate a new token, replace the stored hash, write the file (overwriting), exit |
| bootstrapped, token file exists | refuse to start: exit 1, naming the file |
| bootstrapped, no token file | start normally; `--admin-email` is ignored |

The token is `parley_admin_` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (§3.3.2). The token file has mode 0600 and holds the token with no trailing newline. After writing it, the server logs the file's absolute path at warn level, tells the operator to save the token and delete the file, and exits with status 0 without serving. The token itself is never logged; the hub stores only its hash. After a reset the old token's hash is gone, so the old token stops working at once. If the token file cannot be written, the process exits 1 naming the file and the stored e-mail and hash are unchanged.

### Maintenance loop (PLAT-FR-005, NFR-043)

The loop runs one pass right after start and then one every hour. The interval is not configurable. A pass runs the registered tasks in this order, skipping a name nobody registered: `retention`, `secret_reencryption`, `claim_cleanup`, `forge_delivery_pruning`, `token_binding_sweep`, `patch_purge`, `fork_expiry`, `sandbox_record_cleanup`. A failing task is logged and does not stop the others. Passes never overlap. The loop is the guaranteed backstop; a section may also act on its own, finer timer.

### Shutdown (PLAT-FR-004)

On SIGTERM or SIGINT the server stops accepting connections and gives in-flight requests 15 seconds to finish. Long-lived responses are told to end at once. Background work stops within the grace its section sets (running rebuild jobs: 30 s). The process exits when requests and background work have ended or their grace has passed, at most 30 s after the signal. Sandboxes are not touched. Anything durable resumes at the next start: what a transaction committed before the signal is there after a restart. A clean shutdown exits 0. A failure to bind the listener exits 1.

### Scrubbing (PLAT-FR-098, NFR-021, NFR-042)

Text that leaves the hub in logs, events, audit records or error messages MUST NOT contain credentials. Before such text is emitted:

- known secret values (tokens, secrets, forge and sandbox runtime credentials) are replaced by `[redacted]`;
- user information is removed from URLs: `https://user:pass@host/…` becomes `https://host/…`;
- the text is cut to at most 1024 bytes on a character boundary;
- if a secret cannot be removed cleanly, the whole text becomes `[redacted]`.

The hub never logs an `Authorization` header or a request body that carries a secret. Every line the hub's logger writes, and the one error line of a failed start, passes through the scrubber.

### Backup (§3.9 "Server flags", NFR-007)

`parleyd backup <directory>` writes a consistent snapshot of the data directory while the hub runs. It reads the same configuration as the server to find the data. The directory must be empty; the command exits 1 when it is not. The snapshot holds the transactional store, the analytical store and the repositories under the workspace root. Each store in the snapshot holds whole transactions only. The hub keeps serving while the command runs.

### End-to-end flows

**First boot.** An operator writes `config.toml` with an OAuth client secret given as `${GITHUB_SECRET}` and runs `parleyd --admin-email=a@x`. `parleyd` loads the configuration, creates the data directory, opens the stores, stores the e-mail and the token's hash, writes `admin_token`, logs its path and exits 0. The operator starts `parleyd` again: it refuses, naming the file. The operator saves the token, deletes the file and starts `parleyd`: it runs the start hooks, starts the maintenance loop, listens and logs the address, the configuration path and the data directory. `GET /readyz` answers 200. The operator sends SIGTERM and `parleyd` exits 0.

**Backup of a running hub.** While `parleyd` serves, the operator runs `parleyd backup /backups/today`. The command reads the configuration, copies both stores and the repositories into the empty directory and exits 0. The running hub still answers `GET /readyz` with 200.

**Hourly maintenance.** The hour passes. `parleyd` starts a pass and runs the registered tasks in the fixed order. One task fails; `parleyd` logs it with the task's name and runs the remaining tasks. The next pass runs an hour later.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; the stores are embedded SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` (no cgo) behind `internal/store`, the analytical store being the same engine in a second file; `parleyd` parses its flags with the standard `flag` package; tests use the standard `testing` package, table-driven, with `net/http/httptest` and `t.TempDir()`.
2. **TOML parser.** `github.com/BurntSushi/toml` v1.6.0, decoding into a generic map that the key registry then checks. Why: strictness is decided by the registry, not by struct tags, because other packages add keys.
3. **Two directories beyond the brief's layout.** `internal/scrub/` is a leaf every package can import without a cycle. `internal/hub/` composes the process, so that `cmd/parleyd` stays a thin `main` and tests and `test/e2e` start a hub in-process.
4. **The run function's inputs.** The hub's run function takes the arguments, an environment lookup, the working directory, stdout and stderr, and returns the exit status. The listen address now comes from configuration; tests set `[server].bind` to `127.0.0.1` and `port` to 0. Why: tests run in parallel without changing the process environment.
5. **Key registry.** The PRD says an unknown key stops the start and also lets a dozen sections define keys. A package registers each key it owns; several packages may register keys in one section (`[limits]`). A duplicate registration is a start error.
6. **Environment references.** Replacement happens after parsing and only in string values. A `$` followed by neither `{` nor `$` stays as it is. `${` without `}`, and a name that does not match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, are invalid values of their key. The PRD is silent on all three.
7. **Config path when the file is missing.** The `config` member of the listening line is the path that was looked for.
8. **Relative paths.** A `database.path` or `workspace.path` with a directory part is resolved against the working directory. A bare file name with `XDG_DATA_HOME` unset is resolved against the working directory too.
9. **Analytical store file.** `analytics.db` in the data directory. The workspace root is created with mode 0700 like the data directory. The mode of a directory that already exists is not changed.
10. **Schema steps.** A step has a unique name, a target store and a function; steps are applied in registration order and the applied names are recorded in the store they target. Registering a name twice is a start error. This is the mechanism only; the compatibility guarantee of NFR-003 is package 54's.
11. **Admin token.** 32 bytes from the system's random source, written as 64 lowercase hex characters after `parley_admin_`. The stored hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the whole token. Package 04 authenticates against it.
12. **Bootstrap corners the PRD leaves open.** `--reset-admin-token` wins over an existing token file (the PRD says it overwrites). With both flags on a hub that is not bootstrapped, the e-mail is stored too. An `--admin-email` with an empty value counts as not given. A token file left over on a hub that is not bootstrapped is overwritten by `--admin-email`. The file is written inside the transaction that stores the hash, so a failed write stores nothing.
13. **Start hooks and background work.** Later packages register a start hook (a function that returns an error) and background work (a function that runs until its context is cancelled, with a grace). Hooks run in registration order; a hook's error stops the start. The first maintenance pass runs in the background and does not delay the listener.
14. **Maintenance details.** The eight task names are fixed by this package. A task registered under any other name runs after the eight, in registration order, so that a package with a cleanup the PRD's table does not list has a place. A task that panics counts as failed. An hourly tick that arrives while a pass runs is dropped; the next pass starts at the next tick. At shutdown no further task starts, the running task's context is cancelled, and the loop is given 15 seconds.
15. **Shutdown details.** The hub offers a shutdown notification that fires when the signal arrives; handlers of long-lived responses end on it. Background work whose grace passes is abandoned. The stores are closed last. The exit status is 0 also when a grace passed, as package 01 decided for requests. A grace above 30 seconds is cut to the 30-second total. A second SIGTERM or SIGINT during the shutdown changes nothing: no grace restarts and the process does not exit early.
16. **Start errors are one JSON log line** at error level on stderr, written through the scrubbing logger.
17. **`trace`** is a level below `debug`; with it every line is written.
18. **How the scrubber knows a secret.** Two ways: values a package registers (configuration secrets such as `client_secret`, forge and runtime credentials, decrypted secrets) and values passed with one call; and the hub's own credential formats, recognised by shape because the hub keeps only their hashes: `parley_admin_<64 hex>`, `parley_pat_<8>_<32>` and `parley_<8>_<32>`. Longer values are replaced first. An empty value, and a value that is a part of the marker `[redacted]`, are ignored.
19. **"Cannot be removed cleanly"** is decided by looking again: if the text after replacement still holds a known secret value, a hub credential or a URL with user information, the whole text becomes `[redacted]`. The order is: replace values, remove user information, look again, cut.
20. **User information in URLs** is everything between `://` and the last `@` before the next `/`, whitespace or end of text, for any scheme.
21. **Backup details.** The snapshot directory holds the database file under its own name, `analytics.db` and the workspace root under its own name. Stores are copied first (each as one consistent read), then the repositories, refs before objects. A directory that does not exist is created; a path that is a file is refused like a non-empty directory. On a failure the command removes what it wrote. It opens no listener, applies no schema step and writes nothing to the data. On success it writes one log line and nothing on stdout. `--admin-email` or `--reset-admin-token` together with `backup` is a usage error (exit 2).
22. **`parleyd backup` supersedes** package 01's refusal of every positional argument, for the word `backup` only (brief, note 2). Package 01 has no criterion and no test about `backup` as first argument, so this package changes none of its tests.
23. **OAuth endpoint defaults.** `github`: `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize`, `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, `https://api.github.com/user`. `google`: `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`, `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`, `https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`. The PRD says "the provider's public endpoints" and shows only GitHub's authorize URL.
24. **Profile: full**, with three execution paths.
25. **Idempotency records are kept in the transactional store** (decided with package 02). The source PRD lists them as "kept for 24 hours, then dropped" and only the rate-limit counters as "in memory; reset at restart" (§3.7). Package 02 defines the record store interface and the replay behaviour; this package, which owns the store and composes the process, registers one schema step for the records and installs a store-backed implementation of that interface through the server option package 02 provides (`internal/hub/idempotency.go`). Why here: no package owns both sides, and this one already hands package 02's server its other options.
26. **Where later packages plug in.** `internal/hub/` is the one place that composes the process: a package registers its configuration keys, schema steps, start hooks, background work, maintenance tasks, routes and the checks of package 02's pipeline positions on the composition, in a file of its own (`internal/hub/identity.go`, `internal/hub/access.go`, `internal/hub/events.go`). `cmd/parleyd/main.go` stays a thin caller and is not edited by later packages. The admin-token code in `internal/identity/admin.go` offers a verification function (a presented token against the stored hash, compared in constant time, false when none is stored) that package 04 authenticates with.
27. **Whole-section registration** (decided with package 44 sandbox_runtime_and_profiles). Beside per-key registration, `internal/config/registry.go` offers `RegisterSection(name, validator)`: the registrant's validator receives the whole parsed section, after environment references are replaced, and its single error, which lists every failure, fails the load; the loaded configuration reports whether the file held the section and its content. Why: the per-key walk stops at the first bad key, and SBX-FR-002 wants every failure of `[sandbox]` together, with tables and lists the key registry does not describe. Package 44 registers `[sandbox]` through it and adds nothing to the loader. A section is registered either key by key or as a whole, never both.

## Dependencies

- Package 01 hub_skeleton (draft): this package extends its run function, its server options, its readiness probes and its shutdown.
- Package 02 http_api_conventions (draft): the server options this package fills from configuration (body limit, requests per minute, health-probe logging), the pipeline positions later packages install their checks in through the composition, and the idempotency record store interface this package implements over the transactional store.

## Verified External API

`github.com/BurntSushi/toml` v1.6.0, read in the module cache (`decode.go`, `meta.go`, `error.go`):

- `func Decode(data string, v any) (MetaData, error)`
- `func (md *MetaData) Keys() []Key`
- `func (k Key) String() string`
- `type ParseError struct` (carries the position of a syntax error)

`modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1, read in the module cache (`sqlite.go`, `driver.go`):

- the driver registers itself with `database/sql` under the name `sqlite` (`sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)`)
- the data source name accepts `_pragma=<name>(<value>)` and `_txlock=<mode>` query parameters

The SQL statement `VACUUM INTO '<file>'` used for the snapshot is SQLite's own and was not exercised here: **unverified** through this driver.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Durable job**: Background work that is recorded before its request returns, survives restarts and is retried with backoff. Rebuilds are the only durable jobs (§10). Clone work, restacks and land attempts are also durable but follow their own rules and are not retried with backoff (§4, §7, §8).

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Configuration file

**Rationale:** An operator configures the hub in one file, and a typing mistake in it must stop the start instead of being ignored.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the configuration is loaded with an environment and a working directory, THE configuration loader SHALL read the file $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set and non-empty and the file config.toml in the working directory otherwise, once, and report the path it used and that path's directory as the config dir
   → the loaded configuration carries the absolute path of the file that was looked for and the config dir; values come from that file and from no other
   Check: unit
   - setup: two temporary directories, work and xdg; the environment is a map passed to the loader, not the process environment
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go, a table over (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, files present) {(unset, work/config.toml with port 1111), ('', work/config.toml with port 1111), (xdg, xdg/config.toml with port 2222 and work/config.toml with port 1111), (xdg, only work/config.toml with port 1111)}: cfg, err = config.Load(env, workDir); assert err == nil; assert cfg.Path == expected absolute path; assert cfg.Dir == dir(cfg.Path); assert cfg.Server.Port == {1111, 1111, 2222, 8080}
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the configuration is loaded and the file does not exist, THE configuration loader SHALL use the default of every key

### REQ-2: Environment references in configuration

**Rationale:** Secrets such as OAuth client secrets are given to the hub through its environment, not written into the file.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a string value of the file contains ${NAME} for a variable that is set, or $$, THE configuration loader SHALL replace each ${NAME} by the value of the environment variable NAME, each $$ by one $, leave a $ that is followed by neither { nor $ as it is, and validate the resulting value as it validates a literal one
   → the loaded value is the replaced text; a variable set to the empty string yields the empty string; the same holds for string values inside [[oauth.providers]] tables and for registered keys of other packages
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/env_test.go, with env {HOST: 'hub.example', SECRET: 's3cr3t', EMPTY: '', LVL: 'debug'}, a table of (file value, key, expected): ('https://${HOST}', server.external_url, 'https://hub.example'), ('${SECRET}', client_secret of a provider, 's3cr3t'), ('a${EMPTY}b${SECRET}', client_id, 'abs3cr3t'), ('pa$$word', client_secret, 'pa$word'), ('$${SECRET}', client_secret, '${SECRET}'), ('cost $5', client_secret, 'cost $5'), ('${LVL}', logging.level, 'debug'), ('${HOST}', a registered string key x.y, 'hub.example'): cfg, err = config.Load(env, dirWith(file)); assert err == nil; assert value == expected
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF a string value contains ${NAME} and the environment has no variable NAME, THEN THE configuration loader SHALL fail the load
   → the load returns no configuration and an error whose text contains the variable's name and the section.key of the value that referred to it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/env_test.go, a table over {('[server]\nexternal_url = "https://${NOPE}"', 'NOPE', 'server.external_url'), (a provider with client_secret '${GH_SECRET}', 'GH_SECRET', 'client_secret')} with an empty environment: cfg, err = config.Load(env{}, dirWith(file)); assert cfg == nil; assert contains(err.Error(), variable) and contains(err.Error(), key)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF a string value contains ${ with no closing }, or ${NAME} where NAME does not match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, THEN THE configuration loader SHALL fail the load as for an invalid value
   → the load returns no configuration and an error whose text contains the section.key of the value
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/env_test.go, a table over values of server.external_url {'https://${HOST', '${}', '${1ST}', '${A B}', '${A-B}'} with env {HOST: 'h'}: cfg, err = config.Load(env, dirWith(file)); assert cfg == nil; assert contains(err.Error(), 'server.external_url')
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE configuration loader SHALL for any value of an environment variable, replace references only inside string values and only after the file has been parsed, so that the variable's content never adds, removes or renames a key or a section and never reaches a key name, an integer or a boolean
   → with a variable whose value holds TOML syntax, the loaded configuration has the same keys as without it, and the string value holds the variable's content byte for byte; an expanded value that is invalid for its key fails the load with an error containing section.key; the error text does not contain the variable's value
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/env_test.go, with env {EVIL: '"\n[server]\nport = 1\n', BAD: 'ftp://x', LVL: 'loud'}: cfg = Load of a file with a provider whose client_secret is '${EVIL}' and no [server] table; assert cfg.Server.Port == 8080; assert provider.ClientSecret == env.EVIL; then a table of invalid expansions {server.external_url = '${BAD}' -> error contains 'server.external_url', logging.level = '${LVL}' -> error contains 'logging.level'}; and a file with the table header '[${LVL}]' -> error (an unknown section named literally '${LVL}')
   ```

### REQ-3: Data directory and stores

**Rationale:** Everything the hub knows lives under one data directory in embedded stores, so that the hub needs no external database and a backup is a copy.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the configuration is loaded, THE store SHALL resolve database.path and workspace.path: the defaults are data/parley.db and data/workspaces under the working directory, or parley.db and workspaces under $XDG_DATA_HOME when XDG_DATA_HOME is set and non-empty; a configured bare file name is placed under $XDG_DATA_HOME when that is set; every other relative path is resolved against the working directory; an absolute path is kept
   → both paths are reported as absolute paths; the data directory is the directory of the database path; the analytical store's path is analytics.db in the data directory
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go, a table of (XDG_DATA_HOME, database.path in file, workspace.path in file) -> (database, workspaces): (unset, none, none) -> (work/data/parley.db, work/data/workspaces); ('', none, none) -> same; (xdg, none, none) -> (xdg/parley.db, xdg/workspaces); (xdg, 'hub.db', 'repos') -> (xdg/hub.db, xdg/repos); (unset, 'hub.db', 'repos') -> (work/hub.db, work/repos); (xdg, 'var/hub.db', 'var/repos') -> (work/var/hub.db, work/var/repos); (xdg, '/abs/hub.db', '/abs/repos') -> unchanged: cfg, _ = config.Load(env, work); assert cfg.Database.Path, cfg.Workspace.Path, cfg.DataDir() == dir(database), cfg.AnalyticsPath() == join(dir(database), 'analytics.db')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN the stores are opened and the data directory or the workspace root does not exist, THE store SHALL create the data directory and the workspace root, with missing parents, each with mode 0700, and create the transactional store at the database path and the analytical store at analytics.db beside it
   → after the open both directories exist with permission bits 0700, both store files exist, and each store answers a query; a directory that existed before keeps the mode it had
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go: st, err = store.Open(ctx, store.Options{DatabasePath: tmp/a/b/parley.db, WorkspaceRoot: tmp/c/workspaces}, noSteps); assert err == nil; assert mode(tmp/a/b) & 0777 == 0700; assert mode(tmp/c/workspaces) & 0777 == 0700; assert exists(tmp/a/b/parley.db) and exists(tmp/a/b/analytics.db); assert st.Ping(ctx) == nil; st.Close(); then with tmp/d created by the test with mode 0750: Open with DatabasePath tmp/d/parley.db; assert mode(tmp/d) & 0777 == 0750
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN the stores are opened with a list of registered schema steps, each with a unique name and a target store, THE store SHALL apply every step the target store has not recorded, in registration order, each in one transaction together with the record of its name, and skip every recorded step
   → after the first open every step ran once, in registration order; a second open with the same list runs none; an open with one more step appended runs only that step and the rows written before it are still there
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go: steps = [main:'t1' creates table a, analytics:'t2' creates table b, main:'t3' inserts a row into a], each appending its name to a slice ran; Open; assert ran == ['t1', 't2', 't3']; Close; ran = []; Open with the same steps; assert ran == []; Close; Open with steps + [main:'t4' adds a column to a]; assert ran == ['t4']; assert the row inserted by t3 is still in a; assert table b exists in the analytical store and not in the transactional one
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a schema step returns an error, or two registered steps have the same name, THEN THE store SHALL roll the failing step back, keep the steps applied before it, apply no later step, and fail the open
   → store.Open returns no store and an error whose text contains the step's name; a later open with a corrected list applies the failed step and the ones after it and none before it; with a duplicated name no step is applied at all
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go: steps = ['ok1' creates table a, 'boom' creates table x then returns an error, 'ok3' creates table c]; st, err = Open; assert st == nil; assert contains(err.Error(), 'boom'); open the file directly with database/sql: assert table a exists, table x does not, table c does not; then Open with 'boom' corrected: assert ran == ['boom', 'ok3']; and Open on a fresh directory with ['dup', 'dup']: assert error contains 'dup' and no table was created
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN a caller runs a function in a transaction of the transactional store, THE store SHALL commit everything the function wrote when it returns nil, and discard everything it wrote when it returns an error or panics, returning that error to the caller
   → after a nil return the rows are visible to the next reader; after an error return or a panic none of the function's rows is visible, the caller receives the function's error (for a panic an error that carries the panic value), and the store accepts the next transaction
   Check: integration
   - setup: an open store with one step that creates table a
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go, a table over function endings {return nil, return errBoom after two inserts, panic('x') after two inserts}: err = st.Tx(ctx, fn); count = rows in table a; assert (err == nil and count == 2) for the first case; assert (errors.Is(err, errBoom) and count == 0) for the second; assert (err != nil and contains(err.Error(), 'x') and count == 0) for the third; then assert st.Tx(ctx, insertOne) == nil
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] THE store SHALL for any two transactions that run at the same time on the transactional store, complete both, without failing either because the other is running
   → 32 goroutines that each run 25 transactions inserting one row all return nil, and the table holds 800 rows afterwards
   Check: integration
   - setup: an open store with one step that creates table a
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go: run 32 goroutines, each calling st.Tx(ctx, insertOne) 25 times and collecting errors; assert no error (in particular no 'database is locked'); assert count(a) == 800
   ```
1. [REQ-3.7] IF the data directory or the workspace root cannot be created, or a store file exists and is not a database the engine can open, THEN THE store SHALL fail the open without creating or changing a store file
   → store.Open returns no store and an error whose text contains the path that failed; a file that was not a database has the same bytes as before
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/store/store_test.go, a table over {DatabasePath under a path whose parent is a regular file, WorkspaceRoot under a path whose parent is a regular file, DatabasePath pointing at a file holding 4096 bytes of the text 'not a database'}: st, err = store.Open(ctx, opts, noSteps); assert st == nil; assert contains(err.Error(), the failing path); for the third case assert the file's bytes are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-3.8] WHILE the hub is listening, THE store SHALL answer GET /readyz with ready while both stores answer a query, and with not ready when either does not
   → HTTP 200 with body {"status":"ready"} while both stores answer; HTTP 503 with body {"status":"not ready"} after a store has been closed; GET /healthz answers 200 in both states
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub is started in-process: hub.Run runs in a goroutine with an environment map, a temporary working directory holding a config.toml with [server] bind '127.0.0.1' and port 0, and buffers as stdout and stderr
   ```
   in internal/hub/hub_test.go: assert get('/readyz').status == 200 and json == {status: 'ready'}; close the analytical store through the handle the test obtained from the hub; r = get('/readyz'); assert r.status == 503 and json(r.body) == {status: 'not ready'}; assert get('/healthz').status == 200; repeat on a second hub closing the transactional store
   ```

### REQ-4: Start sequence, flags and logging

**Rationale:** An operator must be able to rely on one start order and on a start that either serves or says in one line why it does not.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] IF parleyd is started with a flag it does not define, with --admin-email and no value, with a positional argument other than backup, or with backup followed by no directory or by more than one, THEN THE parleyd SHALL print its usage on stderr and exit without loading configuration, opening data or listening
   → exit status 2; stderr holds the usage text, which names --admin-email, --reset-admin-token and backup <directory>; stdout is empty; no file or directory is created in the working directory or the config dir
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go, replacing the row ['backup', 'dir'] of the existing rejected-arguments table of package 01, a table over args {['--nope'], ['-x'], ['serve'], ['--admin-email'], ['backup'], ['backup', 'a', 'b'], ['backup', 'a', '--nope']}: code = run(ctx, args, env{}, emptyDir, stdout, stderr); assert code == 2; assert contains(stderr, '--admin-email') and contains(stderr, '--reset-admin-token') and contains(stderr, 'backup <directory>'); assert stdout == ''; assert listDir(emptyDir) == []
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN an operator runs parleyd --help, THE parleyd SHALL print usage that names both flags and the backup subcommand on stdout and exit
   → exit status 0; stdout names --admin-email, --reset-admin-token and backup <directory>; stderr is empty; no file or directory is created
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go, extending the --help test of package 01: code = run(ctx, ['--help'], env{}, emptyDir, stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; assert contains(stdout, '--admin-email') and contains(stdout, '--reset-admin-token') and contains(stdout, 'backup <directory>'); assert stderr == ''; assert listDir(emptyDir) == []
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN parleyd is started with no subcommand, THE parleyd SHALL load and validate the configuration, then open the data, then run the bootstrap, then run every registered start hook in registration order, each to completion, then start the maintenance loop, and only then bind the listener on [server].bind and [server].port
   → each stage begins after the stage before it has finished; when the first start hook runs the stores are open and migrated; no TCP connection to the listen address is accepted before the last start hook has returned; the first maintenance pass starts after the last start hook and does not have to finish before the listener is bound
   Check: integration

   ```

   → exactly one line with msg 'listening'; addr carries the port the operating system chose when [server].port is 0; config is the absolute path that was looked for, also when the file does not exist; data_dir is the absolute directory of database.path; a TCP connection to addr is accepted
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/hub_test.go, extending what cmd/parleyd/main_test.go of package 01 asserts for the listening line, a table over {config.toml present in XDG_CONFIG_HOME with port 0 and database.path set, no config file and the environment giving XDG_DATA_HOME (the default port 8080 replaced through a test option)}: rec = json(the line with msg 'listening'); assert count of such lines == 1; assert rec.addr has host and a port != 0; assert rec.config == absolute expected path; assert rec.data_dir == absolute dir of the database path; assert get('http://' + rec.addr + '/healthz').status == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF any stage before listening fails: the configuration is invalid, the data cannot be opened, a schema step fails, the bootstrap refuses, a start hook returns an error, or the listener cannot be bound, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the start at that stage, run no later stage, close what was opened, and exit
   → exit status 1; stderr holds exactly one non-empty line, a JSON object at level error whose text names the cause (the configuration key, the path, the step, the token file, the hook's name or the listen address); no line with msg 'listening' is written; a start hook registered after the failing one is not called

### REQ-5: First-boot admin token

**Rationale:** The operator needs a credential to administer a hub that has no users yet, and that credential must exist in clear text only in a file the operator removes.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN parleyd is started without --admin-email and without --reset-admin-token on a hub that has no admin token hash stored and no token file, THE parleyd SHALL start and serve without creating an admin token
   → the listening line is written; no file admin_token exists in the config dir; the store holds no admin token hash and no admin e-mail
   Check: integration
   ```

### REQ-6: Hourly maintenance loop

**Rationale:** Retention and cleanup must happen without an operator, and one broken task must not stop the rest.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN the maintenance loop is started, THE maintenance loop SHALL run one pass at once and one further pass at each tick of its timer, whose interval is one hour and is not read from configuration
   → one pass has run before the first tick; each tick that arrives while no pass runs starts exactly one pass; the loop's default interval is 1 hour and no configuration key changes it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a registry with one counting task; the loop's ticks come from a channel the test owns
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go: loop = maintenance.New(reg, logger); ticks = make(chan time.Time); go loop.Run(ctx, ticks); wait until the counting task ran once; send a tick; wait; assert count == 2; send a tick; assert count == 3; assert maintenance.Interval == time.Hour; and in internal/config/config_test.go the unknown-key table already refuses '[maintenance]\ninterval = "1m"'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN a pass runs, THE maintenance loop SHALL run the registered tasks one after the other in the order retention, secret_reencryption, claim_cleanup, forge_delivery_pruning, token_binding_sweep, patch_purge, fork_expiry, sandbox_record_cleanup, skip a name nobody registered, and then run every task registered under another name in registration order
   → the order of task calls in a pass is the fixed order above regardless of the order of registration; a task starts only after the task before it has returned; each registered task is called exactly once per pass
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go, a table over registration orders {the eight names reversed, ['fork_expiry', 'extra_b', 'retention', 'extra_a'], ['extra_a'] alone, none}: each task appends its name to a log and asserts that no other task is running; run one pass; assert log == {the eight in the fixed order, ['retention', 'fork_expiry', 'extra_b', 'extra_a'], ['extra_a'], []}
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] IF a task returns an error or panics during a pass, THEN THE maintenance loop SHALL log the failure with the task's name and go on with the next task of the pass, and with the next pass at the next tick
   → one log line at level ERROR with the members task (the task's name) and error (the scrubbed error text or panic value); every task after the failing one is called in the same pass; the process does not exit; the next tick starts a pass in which the failing task is called again
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go, a table over failures of 'claim_cleanup' {returns errors.New('db gone https://u:p@h/x'), panics with 'kaboom'} with 'retention' before it and 'fork_expiry' after it: run a pass; assert log == ['retention', 'claim_cleanup', 'fork_expiry']; rec = the logged line with level 'ERROR'; assert rec.task == 'claim_cleanup'; assert contains(rec.error, 'db gone https://h/x') or contains(rec.error, 'kaboom'); assert not contains(rec.error, 'u:p'); send a tick; assert 'claim_cleanup' was called a second time
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHILE a pass is running, THE maintenance loop SHALL start no second pass, and drop a tick that arrives before the pass has ended
   → at no time do two passes run; a tick during a pass starts nothing, also after the pass has ended; the first tick after the pass has ended starts the next pass
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go: the single task counts its calls, records the highest number of concurrent calls and blocks until released; start the loop (pass 1 blocks); send two ticks without blocking the sender; release the task; wait 50 ms; assert calls == 1; send a tick; wait until calls == 2; assert the highest number of concurrent calls == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] IF two tasks are registered under the same name, or a task is registered with an empty name, THEN THE maintenance loop SHALL refuse the registration
   → the registration returns an error whose text contains the name; the registry holds the first task only; a hub whose composition makes such a registration exits with status 1 and one error line before listening
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go, a table over second registrations {'retention' twice, 'extra' twice, ''}: err = reg.Register(name, fn2); assert err != nil and contains(err.Error(), name); run a pass; assert fn2 was not called; and in internal/hub/hub_test.go: a hub composed with a duplicate registration returns exit status 1 with one stderr line containing the name and no listening line
   ```
1. [REQ-6.6] WHEN the loop's context is cancelled while a pass runs, THE maintenance loop SHALL cancel the context of the running task, start no further task of the pass and no further pass, and return when the running task has returned
   → the running task observes its context as done; the tasks after it in the order are not called; Run returns within 1 second of the task's return; a tick sent after the cancellation starts nothing
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/maintenance/loop_test.go: 'retention' blocks on ctx.Done() and then returns ctx.Err(); 'fork_expiry' appends to the log; start the loop; wait until 'retention' runs; cancel; assert Run returned within 1 s; assert log does not contain 'fork_expiry'; assert no ERROR line is logged for a task that ended with the cancellation
   ```

### REQ-7: Bounded shutdown

**Rationale:** A restart or upgrade must take a known time, and nothing durable may be lost by it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN parleyd receives SIGTERM or SIGINT while it is listening, THE parleyd SHALL stop accepting connections, fire the shutdown notification, cancel the context of every registered piece of background work and of the maintenance loop, wait for in-flight requests for at most 15 seconds and for each piece of background work for at most its registered grace, close the stores after both, and exit
   → exit status 0; every piece of background work saw its context cancelled and had returned before the stores were closed; a TCP connection to the listen address is refused afterwards; with nothing in flight the exit comes within 1 second of the signal
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/shutdown_test.go, a table over signals {SIGTERM, SIGINT} delivered to the test process: register background work w (grace 2 s) that waits for ctx.Done(), then checks st.Ping(ctx2) == nil and records 'w-stopped'; start the hub; send the signal; code = wait for Run (fail after 1 s); assert code == 0; assert 'w-stopped' recorded and its ping succeeded; assert net.Dial(addr) fails; assert st.Ping fails with a closed-store error afterwards
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF a piece of background work has not returned when its registered grace has passed, or requests and background work together are still running 30 seconds after the signal, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop waiting for it, close the stores and exit
   → exit status 0; the exit comes no later than 1 second after the longest grace that applied and never later than 31 seconds after the signal; a registered grace above 30 seconds is treated as 30 seconds
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/shutdown_test.go, with the hub's time limits scaled through test options (request grace 150 ms, total 300 ms; the defaults are asserted to be 15 s and 30 s), a table of (background work, expected exit window): (ignores its context, grace 100 ms) -> [100 ms, 1100 ms); (ignores its context, grace 10 min) -> [300 ms, 1300 ms); (a request handler that never returns, no background work) -> [150 ms, 1150 ms): t0 = now; cancel the hub's context; code = wait for Run; assert code == 0; assert now - t0 inside the window
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN the signal arrives while a handler holds a long-lived response open and watches the hub's shutdown notification, THE parleyd SHALL fire the notification at the moment the signal is handled, before the 15-second request grace starts to run out, so that the handler ends its response
   → the client's response ends with the status the handler set and without a connection error; the process exits with status 0 within 1 second of the signal, not after the request grace
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/shutdown_test.go: register a test route whose handler writes 200 and a first chunk, then blocks on hub.ShuttingDown() and returns; start the hub with the default 15 s request grace; open the stream and read the first chunk; t0 = now; cancel the hub's context; assert the client reads EOF with no error; code = wait for Run; assert code == 0 and now - t0 < 1 s
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any transaction that was committed before the signal, keep its effect across the stop and the next start
   → after a stop by signal and a new start on the same data directory, every row committed before the signal is read back, and every registered start hook is called again at the new start
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/shutdown_test.go: start the hub with a schema step creating table a and a start hook that counts its calls; commit 100 rows through st.Tx; cancel the hub's context right after the last commit returns; wait for exit status 0; start a second hub on the same directories; assert count(a) == 100; assert the hook was called twice in total
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] IF a second SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives while the shutdown is in progress, THEN THE parleyd SHALL go on with the shutdown that is in progress, without restarting any grace
   → exit status 0; the exit comes no later than it would have come without the second signal
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/hub/shutdown_test.go, through cmd/parleyd's run function with time limits scaled as above: background work that ignores its context with grace 200 ms; send SIGTERM to the test process; 50 ms later send SIGINT; code = wait for run; assert code == 0; assert elapsed since the first signal in [200 ms, 1200 ms)
   ```

### REQ-8: Scrubbing credentials from text

**Rationale:** A log line, an event or an error message is read by people and systems that must never receive a credential.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN text is scrubbed and it contains a secret value that was registered with the scrubber or passed with the call, THE scrubber SHALL replace every occurrence of every such value by [redacted], replacing a longer value before a shorter one, and ignoring an empty value and a value that is a part of the text [redacted]
   → the result contains [redacted] at each place a value stood and none of the values; text without a value is returned unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, with registered values {'hunter2-token', 'hunter2', '', 'red'} and a per-call value 'once-only', a table of (input, expected): ('auth failed for hunter2', 'auth failed for [redacted]'), ('hunter2 and hunter2-token', '[redacted] and [redacted]'), ('x once-only y', 'x [redacted] y'), ('nothing here', 'nothing here'), ('a red door', 'a red door'), ('', ''): assert s.Scrub(input, perCall...) == expected; and assert s.Scrub('x once-only y') == 'x once-only y' when the value is not passed
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN text is scrubbed and it contains a credential in one of the hub's own formats, registered or not, THE scrubber SHALL replace each admin token (parley_admin_ and 64 lowercase hex characters), each personal access token (parley_pat_, 8 characters of [a-z0-9], _, 32 characters of [a-z0-9]) and each API key (parley_, 8 characters of [0-9A-Za-z], _, 32 characters of [0-9A-Za-z]) by [redacted]
   → the result contains none of the credentials and [redacted] in the place of each; words that only start like a credential are kept
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, a table of (input, expected) built from generated credentials A (admin), P (PAT), K (API key): ('token ' + A + ' rejected', 'token [redacted] rejected'), ('Bearer ' + P, 'Bearer [redacted]'), ('key=' + K + ';', 'key=[redacted];'), (A + ' ' + P + ' ' + K, '[redacted] [redacted] [redacted]'), ('parley_admin_token is a file', unchanged), ('parley_pat_short_1', unchanged), ('see parley_docs', unchanged): assert scrub.New().Scrub(input) == expected
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN text is scrubbed and it contains a URL with user information, THE scrubber SHALL remove the user information, which is everything between :// and the last @ that comes before the next /, whitespace or end of text, together with that @, for any scheme and for every such URL in the text
   → https://user:pass@host/path becomes https://host/path; the rest of the URL and of the text is kept byte for byte; a URL without user information and an @ outside a URL authority are kept
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, a table of (input, expected): ('https://user:pass@host/x', 'https://host/x'), ('fatal: unable to access https://x-token:abc@github.com/o/r.git/: 403', 'fatal: unable to access https://github.com/o/r.git/: 403'), ('ssh://git@host:22/r', 'ssh://host:22/r'), ('http://u@h', 'http://h'), ('https://user:p@ss@host/x', 'https://host/x'), ('a https://u:p@h1/ b https://v:q@h2/ c', 'a https://h1/ b https://h2/ c'), ('https://host/a@b', unchanged), ('mail bob@example.com', unchanged), ('https://host/x', unchanged): assert scrub.New().Scrub(input) == expected
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN text is scrubbed and the result of the replacements is longer than 1024 bytes, THE scrubber SHALL cut the result to the longest prefix of at most 1024 bytes that ends on a character boundary of its UTF-8 encoding
   → the result is at most 1024 bytes long and is valid UTF-8 when the input was; a result of exactly 1024 bytes is not cut; the cut is applied after the replacements, so a secret that starts before byte 1024 of the input never survives in part
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, a table of (input, expected length): (1024 x 'a', 1024), (1025 x 'a', 1024), (1023 x 'a' + 'é' (2 bytes), 1023), (1022 x 'a' + '€' (3 bytes) + 'z', 1022), (1021 x 'a' + '€', 1024), (5000 x 'é', 1024): out = Scrub(input); assert len(out) == expected; assert utf8.ValidString(out); assert hasPrefix(input, out); and with registered value V = 'SECRETSECRET': out = Scrub(1018 x 'a' + V + 'tail'); assert not contains(out, 'SECRET'); assert len(out) <= 1024
   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] IF the text, after the replacements and the removal of user information, still contains a registered or passed secret value, a credential in one of the hub's formats or a URL with user information, THEN THE scrubber SHALL discard the text and return the marker alone
   → the result is exactly [redacted]
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, a table of (registered values, input): ({'mid', 'x[redacted]y'}, 'say xmidy now') where replacing the first value produces the second; ({'https://h/secretpath'}, 'go https://u:p@h/secretpath') where removing the user information produces a registered value: assert Scrub(input) == '[redacted]'
   ```
1. [REQ-8.6] THE scrubber SHALL for any text and any set of registered values, return a result that is at most 1024 bytes long, contains no registered value that the scrubber does not ignore, no credential in one of the hub's formats and no URL user information, and that scrubbing a second time leaves unchanged
   → len(Scrub(t)) <= 1024; Scrub(Scrub(t)) == Scrub(t); no registered value of the generated set that is not empty and not a part of [redacted] occurs in Scrub(t)
   Check: property
   ```
   in internal/scrub/scrub_test.go, with testing/quick or a seeded generator over 2000 cases: values = 0 to 5 random strings of 1 to 40 bytes over the alphabet 'abc[]redt:/@ é'; t = a random concatenation of 0 to 300 pieces drawn from {a value, a generated admin token, PAT or API key, 'https://u:p@h/x', random text over the same alphabet}; out = Scrub(t); assert len(out) <= 1024; assert Scrub(out) == out; for each value v that is not empty and not a substring of '[redacted]': assert not contains(out, v); assert no hub credential pattern and no '://…@' authority matches in out
   ```
1. [REQ-8.7] WHILE the hub runs, THE scrubber SHALL pass the message and every string attribute of every log line, and the one error line of a failed start, through the scrubber before writing them, with the client_secret of every configured OAuth provider registered as a secret value, and write no Authorization header and no request body to the log
   → a log line emitted with a registered value, a hub credential or a URL with user information in its message or in an attribute shows [redacted] or the stripped URL in their place; a failed start whose error text contains a configured client_secret shows [redacted]; attribute keys and the members time and level are unchanged
   Check: integration

   in internal/hub/logging_test.go: s = scrub.New(); s.Add('hunter2'); log = hub.NewLogger(buffer, 'info', s); log.Info('clone failed for https://u:hunter2@h/r.git', 'err', 'bad token ' + generatedPAT, 'attempt', 3); rec = json(line); assert rec.msg == 'clone failed for https://h/r.git'; assert rec.err == 'bad token [redacted]'; assert rec.attempt == 3; and in internal/hub/hub_test.go: start a hub whose config.toml has a provider with client_secret '${GH}' (env GH = 'topsecret-value') and a start hook returning errors.New('provider said: topsecret-value'); assert exit status 1; assert not contains(stderr, 'topsecret-value'); assert contains(stderr, '[redacted]')
